# Sales Contractor Agreement — Key Terms Acknowledgment

**DRAFT — pairs with `DANI_SALES_CONTRACTOR_AGREEMENT_DRAFT.md`; attorney
review required before use.**

Purpose: put the handful of terms people actually get burned by in plain
language, in front of the full agreement, so nobody signs the legal version
having only skimmed it. If anything here conflicts with the full agreement,
the full agreement controls. Each section gets its own initials line so
there's a record of what was actually walked through, not just a single
signature at the bottom.

---

**1. This engages you as a contractor, not an employee.**
No tax withholding, no benefits — you carry your own insurance and equipment,
and this document doesn't by itself make you an employee. But calling it a
contractor role doesn't settle the legal question either: that depends on how
the relationship actually runs (training, required call methods, coaching,
DANI-approved leads and pricing all count as factors), not on this label. If
anything about how this actually operates feels more like a job with a set
schedule and someone directing your every move than an independent business,
say so — that's a real classification question, not just paperwork.

Initials: __________

**2. How and when you get paid.**
[Fill in from the current compensation schedule: base/commission structure,
payment frequency, and what happens if a pay period is partial.] Payment runs
through DANI's contractor payroll onboarding (direct deposit + W-9) — you're
responsible for completing that accurately.

Initials: __________

**3. Training, if any, is paid for time you actually spend in it.**
If DANI ends training early, you still keep what you already earned for the
days you trained. Training being paid or unpaid, and for how long, will be
stated to you in writing before it starts — if nobody has told you that in
writing, ask before assuming.

Initials: __________

**4. What you can and can't say on a call.**
You represent DANI's real pricing, real policies, and real availability —
never manufactured urgency, never a fake "exception" discount, never talking
someone out of taking time to decide or asking for something in writing. This
protects the customer and it protects you personally, since telemarketing law
can hold the individual caller responsible, not just the company.

Initials: __________

**5. Payment collection never goes through voice or chat.**
You never take, write down, or repeat a customer's card number, CVV, or bank
details over the phone or in any chat tool — that's DANI policy regardless of
what's technically permitted elsewhere, and CVVs specifically must never be
stored after a charge goes through. Where DANI's secure checkout link is
available for the sale you're closing, send it and the customer pays there.
Not every service has that link yet (it's currently limited to certain
resident-concierge sales) — for anything else, escalate to DANI's ops contact
for the proper process. You never work around either case by keying a card
number in yourself.

Initials: __________

**6. Confidentiality.**
Customer, lead, and pricing information you see doing this work stays inside
DANI-approved systems, used only to do the work — during the engagement and
after it ends.
